bridge.title: Four things I noticed

beats.title: 4,872 traders in your Discord. The only thing to buy is a discount code.
beats.text: You trade live every weekday, your channel has 13.7K subscribers, and DamnPropFirms has become a real resource. But there's no DGT product. Everything your audience spends goes to the prop firms, and code DGT is the only way you take part in it.

beats.title: They already watch you trade for hours.
beats.text: 681 videos, live sessions most weekday mornings, 901 people online in your Discord when I checked, and a Chrome extension that applies your code. That's an audience that already trusts your process. It just has no way to learn it from you directly.

beats.title: The prop firms set your terms.
beats.text: Affiliate income depends on firms you don't control: their rules, their payouts, their commission. When a firm changes or disappears, so does that part of the business. A program of your own is the one piece nobody else can change.

beats.title: “No fake gurus.” That's exactly why it works.
beats.text: Fake gurus hide their trades. You show all of them live, wins and losses. A mentorship built on that same transparency is the opposite of a guru course, and the application keeps out anyone looking for a shortcut.
beats.quote: “Built by a funded futures trader. No corporate team. No paid placements. No fake gurus.”

bridge.closing: So instead of explaining it, I built it. The page, the application, the emails and the ads, all below.

preCallEmails.subject: You're booked: here's what happens next
preCallEmails.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

Your call is booked for {{call_time}}. The link is in your calendar invite.

Before we talk:
1. Keep the time free.
2. Note which prop firms and account types you trade, and have a few recent trades ready.

One note: nobody on my team will ever ask you to pay through a DM. Payments only happen through the official links from this email address.

Talk soon,
Kyle

preCallEmails.subject: Trade the account, not just the chart
preCallEmails.previewText: Why a plan beats one more tip
preCallEmails.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

Most traders blow prop firm accounts on rules, not on bad entries: a trailing drawdown they didn't plan for, a consistency rule they forgot.

The mentorship starts there: the firm's rules first, then a session plan that fits them, then execution.

On the call we'll look at where you are today.

Kyle

preCallEmails.subject: "I already watch the live streams"
preCallEmails.previewText: Then this is the next step
preCallEmails.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

Good. Then you've seen how I trade.

The mentorship is for when watching isn't enough: you get a plan for your own accounts and I review how you actually trade it.

If you're not sure you need it, ask on the call. We'll tell you honestly.

Kyle

preCallEmails.subject: What we'll cover on the call
preCallEmails.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

The call takes about 30 minutes:

1. Where you are now and what you've tried.
2. Where you want to be in a year.
3. How the program works, what it costs, and whether it fits you.

If it isn't a fit, we'll tell you. No pressure either way.

Kyle

preCallEmails.subject: Tomorrow: your call with Kyle's team
preCallEmails.body:
Hey {{first_name}},

Quick reminder: your call is tomorrow at {{call_time}}.

If the time doesn't work anymore, reschedule with the link in your invite so someone else can take the slot.

See you tomorrow,
Kyle
